description:
When did a given flight depart on a given UTC date, on which tail and type, and to where?

Looks a callsign up in the capture for the UTC date of its actual wheels-up and returns each
matching flight with departure and destination, filed registration and ICAO type, the chosen
actual wheels-up time, how long the feed carried it, and flags where the messages disagreed
(conflicting wheels-up values, other callsigns or tails seen, a destination amended in flight).
`departure` (ICAO, or a three-letter code read as its K- form) narrows it. If nothing departed
that date, `nearest_dates_with_this_callsign` and `plans_without_wheels_up` say what was seen
instead -- a plan filed but never airborne in the feed was cancelled, not flown, or not captured.


NOT FOR OPERATIONAL USE: Airside Labs' historic capture of the FAA SWIM SFDPS flight feed, for reference and analysis; redistributed by Airside Labs and not endorsed by the FAA. Say so when you quote it. SCOPE: departures from KJFK and KEWR (from 13 Aug 2026) and KSEA (from 16 Sep 2026) only -- the subscription's filter; other airports appear only as destinations. Times are UTC and a flight belongs to the UTC date of its actual wheels-up (a US evening departure is often the next UTC date). Callsigns are ICAO-style (UAL149, DAL168) or a registration for private flights. Reading the answer: `status` is resolved, none_found (the airport and date are captured and nothing matched; read `capture_warning` if present -- a thin day or a feed gap weakens that), not_captured (the date is outside the capture or the departure airport is not in scope -- never evidence that nothing flew), unresolved (the input could not be used; the note says why) or unavailable. `registration` and `icao_type` are as filed in the flight plan: a tail can be swapped before departure. `wheels_up_conflict` shows when messages disagreed; `possible_duplicate_of` marks a plan the FAA re-issued for a flight already airborne. `provenance` cites the capture edition. For which tails usually fly a flight over time, use flight_airframes.
name: flight_departure_lookup
title: Look up a captured departure
